reason: No closure or corpus entry covers relation-matrix full-rank or degree-variance shaping; the closest are TREAT-summation-cover-monodromy (scope_limits list VARIANCE of yield as left free), LEAD-ICB-orbit-linear-algebra (LA is 0.0-2.7% of S, so a relation-count saving moves no end-to-end board), and corpus KN-OPEN-006 (LA-stage only). The mechanism itself is textbook: the full-rank threshold of sparse random matrices depends on the row/column degree distribution (Blomer-Karp-Welzl 1997; Cooper 2000; Dubois-Mandler 3-XORSAT m/n~2.75; Coja-Oghlan et al, The rank of sparse random matrices, RSA 2023; Full rank condition for sparse random matrices, CPC 2024) and index-calculus relation-count heuristics (LaMacchia-Odlyzko; ratio ~2.0 in structured Gaussian elimination) are standard. Cited prior art 2506.00429 is 'Combinatorial t-Designs from Finite Abelian Groups and Elliptic Curve Codes' (Liu-Tang-Fan-Luo): a design-construction paper, not a relation-rank result. The idea therefore cannot be called an advance: expected class accounting is right. Uncovered part: whether a choice of F can control per-base-point degree variance. Mean degree is fixed by monodromy/conservation, but over F_r the matrix needs only >=B rows, so the gain is bounded by the coverage overhead (coupon collector ~ln B/(m+1) x B: about 2.3x at B=1024, m=2, falling to 1 + o(1) once relations exceed the min-degree requirement) and by the large-prime/structured-Gaussian-elimination practice that already trades this off. Not measured in the programme.
